citation: An Act fixing the military peace establishment of the United States, ch. 9, 16 March 1802; United States Statutes at Large, vol. 2, p. 132
describes_date: the peace establishment in force from 1 June 1802, under which the first Fort Dearborn was built and garrisoned (1803-1812)
rights_note: An Act of Congress, printed in the official Statutes at Large. Edicts of government are not copyrightable in the United States.
access_notes: Read on 2026-11-03 for T-3332 from the govinfo page of 2 Stat. 132 (sec. 6 on printed p. 134) and checked against the American Battlefield Trust's transcription; the two agree word for word on the ration.
what_it_supplies: THE GARRISON'S CANDLES: sec. 6, 'That each ration shall consist of one pound and a quarter of beef, or three quarters of a pound of pork, eighteen ounces of bread or flour, one gill of rum, whiskey or brandy, and at the rate of two quarts of salt, four quarts of vinegar, four pounds of soap, and one pound and a half of candles to every hundred rations.' A soldier's quarters were lit by issued candles, at about a quarter of an ounce of candle a man a day.
what_it_does_not_supply: how the candles were burned: which rooms, at which hours, or whether lanterns were kept at the gate or the guard
the number of rations drawn at Fort Dearborn on any day
note: Written for T-3332 (1812 by night). The ration is the law, not a return from the post; it says what the issue was, so the fort's windows are lit by candle, and lit sparingly.
